For articles, if the article is badly written or is filled with incorrect facts, then you might downvote it. But as most of these subs are new, there isn't very much to evaluate.

I've often thought downvotes are used to suppress more than anything else (can anyone say hivemind?). If a submission or comment should be removed for rule violation then we just need to be more active in reporting spam etc and let that mechanic do its job. Only allowing upvotes means (in theory) the most valued content rises to the top anyway and with no downvotes unpopular submissions can't be hidden away to create an echo chamber where no one sees any conflicting opinions.

I think there's merit to the concept of downvotes being used to deal with posts that don't technically break any rules, but also don't add to the discussion, or that actively detract from it. The problem is that that's not what most people seem to use downvotes for, so in the case of removing them entirely, it might just be a "This is why we can't have nice things." sort of situation.

There is definitely merit to downvoting non-constructive posts that don't technically break site rules...ayy lamo, this. just the tip, m'emetics of all kinds really... I've seen so many threads on important topics have their discussions completely derailed by them. That said, I think I'd rather see subs have their own policy on that sort of content because historically downvotes have not so much been used to filter out the low quality as they have been used to punish dissenting opinions. Despite the rules, we all know it is an "I disagree button". The trouble there is, then you have to decide what is quality control and what is stifling expression, and from our experience at reddit someone is going to overstep that mark and start deleting "low quality" comments on their sub because they just don't like what was said or the person who said it.

I guess what it comes down to is I want us to be a self policing community, capable of behaving like mature people, acting appropriately to the sub we are posting in and discouraging those that don't, but when it comes down to it we're anonymous internet users and that pretty much means we're going to have lowest common denominator posts rising to the top and controversial content getting silenced with downvotes with no way to keep the the trolls, white knights and power hungry mods out.
